newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm on fund-related buying, beans.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm on fund-related buying, beans.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat settled mostly higher and well above their intraday lows on fund-related buying in the July contract and on spillover strength from CBOT soybeans and corn, traders said.

"Fund selling in (CBOT wheat) dried up by the midsession and fund-related buying actually developed here in Kansas City. The price action in beans and corn didn't hurt," a KCBT trader said. "It sort of leaves me with the feeling that maybe our weekly lows are in place."
KCBT wheat ended 10 cents per bushel lower to seven cents higher, with July up 6-1/4 cents at $3.95-1/4.
The only contract to close lower was September 1998, which lost 10 cents to end at $3.75.

KCBT wheat spent much of the session flip-flopping around the unchanged mark. But wheat gathered momentum as Refco, a brokerage commonly linked to fund-related activity, bought the July contract. Refco bought 3.3 million July on the day, traders said.
A double-digit rally in old crop CBOT soybeans also boosted wheat. Traders said soybeans surged on signs the market was oversold and on export rumors.
